description: Savor the true taste of Liguria with this authentic Focaccia Genovese, a beloved Italian flatbread. Its irresistibly soft interior, crispy crust, and signature dimples are generously infused with fragrant rosemary and the finest olive oil. Perfect for dipping, as a side, or a delightful snack, this recipe brings Italian tradition right to your table.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and granulated sugar. Sprinkle the active dry yeast over the top and let it sit for 3-5 minutes until it becomes foamy. This indicates the yeast is active and ready to use.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Gradually incorporate 30ml of the extra virgin olive oil until it is mostly absorbed into the dough.

instructions.title: Knead and First Rise
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. It should still be slightly sticky. Form the dough into a ball, place it in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape the Focaccia
instructions.text: Lightly grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan with 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Gently punch down the risen dough to release air and transfer it to the prepared pan. Using your fingertips, gently stretch and press the dough to evenly fill the pan. Cover again and let rise for another 30-45 minutes.

instructions.title: Dimple and Top
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the surface of the dough. Drizzle generously with the remaining olive oil, then sprinkle with the fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake and Serve
instructions.text: Bake for 20-35 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and cooked through. The internal temperature should be around 200-210°F (93-99°C). Let cool slightly in the pan before transferring to a wire rack. Slice into generous pieces and serve warm.

tips: For truly authentic Genovese focaccia, use a high-quality extra virgin olive oil from Liguria. It makes a significant difference in the flavor and texture.
Dont be afraid to be generous with the olive oil before baking; it is key to the focaccias crispy exterior and tender crumb. You can also add thinly sliced onions or olives for variation.
Focaccia is best enjoyed warm on the day it is baked. If you have leftovers, refresh them in a hot oven for a few minutes before serving to restore their crispness.
article:
The aroma of freshly baked bread, the subtle sweetness of olive oil, and the fragrant whisper of rosemary – these are the hallmarks of true Italian baking. Among the pantheon of Italy’s beloved breads, one stands out for its elegant simplicity and irresistible texture: Focaccia Genovese. This isn't just any focaccia; it's a regional masterpiece from Genoa, the capital of Liguria, where the sea breeze and olive groves define the culinary landscape. Infused with the purest extra virgin olive oil and fragrant rosemary, Focaccia Genovese offers a unique experience – a crispy bottom, an airy, open crumb, and a beautifully dimpled surface that cradles golden pools of olive oil and sparkling sea salt. Preparing this traditional bread at home is a journey into the heart of Italian comfort food, promising a reward far greater than the effort.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?

Focaccia Genovese is a distinct variety of focaccia originating from Genoa, Italy, renowned for its specific characteristics that set it apart from other Italian flatbreads. Unlike its thicker, often more bread-like cousins found elsewhere, the Genovese version is typically flatter, boasts an incredibly crisp base, and features a remarkably light, airy, and open crumb structure. The secret to its texture lies in a high-hydration dough and a generous hand with Ligurian extra virgin olive oil – both in the dough and drizzled lavishly on top before baking.

The surface of authentic Focaccia Genovese is unmistakable: it's deeply dimpled, creating small wells that capture olive oil, forming glistening pockets of flavour during baking. These dimples also contribute to its characteristic texture, preventing the dough from rising too much and ensuring a uniform crispness. While many focaccias can be piled with various toppings, traditional Focaccia Genovese is celebrated for its minimalist approach, typically seasoned only with coarse sea salt and fresh rosemary, allowing the quality of the olive oil and the bread itself to shine. It’s often enjoyed for breakfast, dipped in coffee or milk, or as a snack throughout the day, a testament to its everyday appeal in Ligurian culture.

## Ingredients for Authentic Focaccia Genovese

Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese begins with selecting the right ingredients. Quality is paramount, especially for a recipe so simple.

*   **Strong Bread Flour (or "00" Flour):** Approximately 500g. A high-protein flour is crucial for developing the gluten structure needed for focaccia's airy crumb. If "00" flour isn't available, a good quality unbleached bread flour will work well.
*   **Lukewarm Water:** About 350-380ml. The exact amount can vary slightly depending on your flour and humidity. It should be warm enough to activate the yeast but not hot (around 35-40°C / 95-105°F).
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** 7g (or 2 ¼ teaspoons). This will give your dough the lift and airy texture characteristic of Focaccia Genovese.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** 10g (about 1 ½ teaspoons) for the dough. Salt is essential for flavour and controlling yeast activity.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** At least 60-80ml for the dough, plus a generous amount (another 50-70ml) for oiling the pan, drizzling on top, and finishing. This is perhaps the most critical ingredient; invest in a good quality, fruity extra virgin olive oil, ideally from Liguria, for authentic flavour.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** A few sprigs, needles stripped and roughly chopped, for infusing flavour and aroma.
*   **Flaky Sea Salt:** For sprinkling on top before baking, adding a delightful crunch and burst of salinity.

## Step-by-Step Focaccia Genovese Recipe

This recipe will guide you through creating a truly memorable Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia Genovese.

**1. Activate the Yeast:** In a small bowl, combine the lukewarm water with the active dry yeast and a pinch of sugar (optional, helps wake up the yeast). Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.

**2. Mix the Dough:** In a large mixing bowl (or the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook), combine the flour and fine sea salt. Pour in the activated yeast mixture and 60ml of the extra virgin olive oil.

**3. Knead the Dough:**
    *   **By Hand:** Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10-15 minutes. The dough will be quite sticky initially due to its high hydration, but resist the urge to add too much extra flour. Keep kneading until it becomes smooth, elastic, and less sticky.
    *   **Stand Mixer:** Mix on low speed for 2-3 minutes until combined, then increase to medium speed and knead for 8-10 minutes. The dough should pull away from the sides of the bowl and be smooth and elastic.

**4. First Rise (Bulk Fermentation):** Lightly grease a clean large bowl with olive oil. Transfer the dough to the bowl, turning it once to coat with oil. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel. Let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

**5. Prepare the Pan:** Generously coat a 30x40 cm (12x16 inch) baking sheet or a similar-sized rectangular pan with at least 3-4 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil. Ensure the entire bottom and sides are well-oiled; this is key for the crispy crust.

**6. Stretch and Dimple the Dough:** Gently deflate the risen dough and carefully transfer it to the prepared baking sheet. Drizzle a little more olive oil over the dough. Using your fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to tear it. If the dough springs back, let it rest for 10-15 minutes, then continue stretching. Once stretched, use your oiled fingertips to create deep dimples across the entire surface of the focaccia, pushing almost to the bottom of the pan. Sprinkle the fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt evenly over the dimpled dough.

**7. Second Rise (Proofing):** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a light tea towel. Let the focaccia rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until it looks puffy and slightly increased in volume.

**8. Preheat Oven:** While the dough is proofing, preheat your oven to a high temperature, around 220-240°C (425-475°F). A hot oven is crucial for achieving that signature crispy crust.

**9. Bake the Focaccia:** Bake for 20-30 minutes, or until the Focaccia Genovese is beautifully golden brown on top and the bottom is crisp and golden.

**10. Finish and Serve:** As soon as you remove the focaccia from the oven, drizzle it generously with a final touch of excellent extra virgin olive oil. This enhances flavour and keeps the crust tender. Let it cool on a wire rack for a few minutes before slicing and serving.

## Tips for Perfect Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia

Achieving the perfect Focaccia Genovese is an art, but these tips will guide you to success:

*   **Invest in Quality Olive Oil:** This cannot be stressed enough. A good extra virgin olive oil is the soul of Focaccia Genovese. It contributes significantly to the flavour, texture, and aroma.
*   **Don't Fear the Stickiness:** Focaccia dough is a high-hydration dough, meaning it's quite wet and sticky. Resist the urge to add too much flour during kneading or stretching, as this will result in a dense, dry focaccia. Embrace the stickiness; oil your hands instead of flouring them when handling.
*   **Generous Oiling of the Pan:** The copious amount of olive oil in the baking pan is what gives Focaccia Genovese its characteristic crispy, golden bottom crust. Don't skimp!
*   **Proper Dimpling:** Use your fingertips to make deep indentations, but don't poke holes through the dough. These dimples are essential for preventing a large air pocket from forming under the crust and for creating little reservoirs for the olive oil and salt.
*   **High Heat Baking:** A very hot oven ensures a quick bake, which helps create a contrast between the crispy exterior and the soft, airy interior. If the oven isn't hot enough, the focaccia might dry out before it fully browns.
*   **Allow for Sufficient Rise Times:** Dough development is crucial. Don't rush the bulk fermentation or the final proof. These stages develop flavour and texture.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** While dried rosemary can be used in a pinch, fresh rosemary offers a far superior aroma and flavour, especially when combined with good olive oil.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Focaccia Genovese is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in countless ways, from a simple snack to an elegant accompaniment.

*   **As a Snack or Appetizer:** Serve warm or at room temperature, perhaps with a small bowl of high-quality olive oil for dipping, or alongside olives, cured meats, and cheeses for an authentic Italian antipasti spread.
*   **With Meals:** It makes an excellent side dish for soups, stews, roasted meats, or grilled fish. Its robust flavour and satisfying texture complement a wide range of main courses.
*   **For Breakfast:** In Genoa, it's traditional to enjoy a slice of Focaccia Genovese dipped in cappuccino or latte – a surprisingly delicious combination of sweet and savoury that you must try!
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill with your favourite sandwich ingredients – prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, roasted vegetables, or a simple smear of pesto.
*   **Wine Pairings:** Pair with a crisp, dry white wine, such as a Vermentino from Liguria or a Sauvignon Blanc. For red wine lovers, a light-bodied red like a young Dolcetto or Barbera would also be a lovely match.

## Common Questions About Focaccia Genovese

**Q: What makes Focaccia Genovese different from other focaccias?**
A: Focaccia Genovese is typically flatter, boasts a crispier base, and has a very airy, open crumb. It's characterized by its generous use of olive oil, deep dimples on the surface, and often a minimalist topping of just rosemary and sea salt, emphasizing the quality of the bread and oil itself.

**Q: Can I use all-purpose flour instead of bread flour?**
A: While bread flour (or Italian "00" flour) is recommended for its higher protein content, which aids in gluten development and creates a chewier, airier crumb, you can use good quality all-purpose flour. Just be aware the texture might be slightly less chewy or open.

**Q: Why is my focaccia dense?**
A: Several factors can lead to dense focaccia: not enough rise time (first or second proof), insufficient kneading (gluten not properly developed), or adding too much flour during the kneading process, which reduces the dough's hydration. Ensure your yeast is active and your kitchen is warm enough for rising.

**Q: How do I store Focaccia Genovese?**
A: Focaccia is best eaten on the day it's baked. However, you can store leftovers tightly wrapped in plastic wrap at room temperature for up to 2 days. To refresh, simply warm it in a preheated oven (180°C/350°F) for 5-10 minutes until crisp again. It can also be frozen, wrapped well, for up to a month.

**Q: Can I add other toppings to my Focaccia Genovese?**
A: While traditional Focaccia Genovese is simple, you can certainly experiment! Cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced onions, olives, or even thinly sliced potatoes are popular additions to other focaccia styles. Just remember that adding too many heavy toppings can weigh down the dough and alter the classic Genovese texture.

Embrace the joy of baking this quintessential Italian bread. The journey from simple ingredients to a golden, aromatic Focaccia Genovese is a rewarding one, bringing a taste of Liguria directly to your kitchen. Buon appetito!
